text.p: Kleinwort Benson said on Friday that it had reiterated its buy stance on the Swedish-U.S. pharmaceuticals group Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc.
Kleinwort analyst Stephen Putnam told Reuters that the company was undervalued by around 30 percent compared to its international peer group.
"We will see credibility and confidence rebuilt during the course of this year," he said.
Kleinwort has an earnings per share forecast of $2.50 for the group in 1998 compared with a prediction of $2.15 this year.

Among factors reinforcing confidence in the newly-merged group, which was hit by profit warnings last year, is the expected announcment of a chief executive to replace John Zabriskie, who departed unexpectedly in Janaury.
Analysts said speculation about the new chief executive had centered on senior managers at the U.S. group Eli Lilly & Co .

Other factors cited by Kleinwort included continued strong performance by two of the group's newest products, colon cancer treatment Camptosar and glaucoma drug Xalatan, which both won U.S. marketing approval in June 1996.
Putnam said he was also optimistic about prospects for incontinence drug Detrusitol, which was filed for approval in Europe last December and in the U.S. in March.
